item.title: Ever since Sony decided to kill off PlayStation discs starting in 2028, the backlash has been pronounced to say the least. And, now, it looks like former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden is also questioning Sony's decision.
item.description:
Ever since Sony decided to kill off PlayStation discs starting in 2028, the backlash has been pronounced to say the least. And, now, it looks like former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden is also questioning Sony's decision.
Last week, Layden was interviewed in an episode of The Expansion Pass podcast, where he was asked about his take on Sony's decision to kill discs. And while he makes it clear that he wasn't in the room for the decision, he prefaces his take by saying "gamers are... yeah, we like the digital download. People said, 'Oh, downloading a game is easier than going to the store!' No, no, downloading a game is easier than going across my living room to put a disc in the machine. I don't even have to do that."
But while digital downloads have always been a win for convenience, Layden said he still believes the decision to kill off discs completely is misguided.
"But I do think, particularly in the gaming realm, maybe 80% of the people download and 20% don't, whatever that breakdown might be, but that's a super important 20%," he said. "I mean, that is largely the most faithful of the faithful, that is, many times, the people who buy two copies of every game, one never gets out of the shrink wrap, and you play the other one."
There are definitely people out there who collect unopened games to put on their shelves, but the bigger issue about this move is the question of ownership. Now, over on PC, we've had to live with this reality for years, thanks to the proliferation of Steam and digital games, but even then, there's at least GOG, which will let you download a game without DRM a lot of the time that you can just archive on your own disc.
But PlayStation will likely never get that option, so the question about ownership is huge, and something that Layden catches onto here.
"It changes the conversation from 'do you own a game, or do you have access to a digital asset?" Layden concluded. "If you can't sell a thing, it means you don't own a thing. If you don't own it, then what are you buying? If you're buying access that doesn't quite sound as sexy, to be honest."
Layden does hit the core of the issue here, and while Sony would likely argue that you were still buying access to a digital access when you were buying the disc, the loss of the tangible item really makes that illusion disappear. From there, it's easy to see why people look at Sony pulling access to movies and imagine that the same is going to happen for their games.
For his part, Layden makes that same connection, noting that, "As people tend to do, in their mind, they'll game out the worst case scenario. And that's a whole lot of brand hit and reputation bite." It certainly was a huge hit to Sony's reputation. Only time will tell, now, whether or not the money Sony saves by not producing discs will be worth the ill will it generated when it killed discs.
Sony does seem intent on making unpopular moves. Earlier this month it filed a couple of patents that would use AI to create vibe-coded patches to fix your PS5, and another that would put an NFC card reader in your controller.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Star Wars actor Jordan Stephens says he declined to return in hit Disney+ series Andor after being told to cut off his dreadlocks — to ensure his appearance looked "realistic."
item.description:
Star Wars actor Jordan Stephens says he declined to return in hit Disney+ series Andor after being told to cut off his dreadlocks to ensure his appearance looked "realistic."
Stephens, better known as half of U.K. rap duo Rizzle Kicks, originally appeared as Rebel Alliance soldier Corporal Tonc in Star Wars: Rogue One. While Tonc died in the movie, he — and many other actors — were invited back for the subsequent prequel series Andor in order to better flesh out his role.
Unfortunately for Stephens, his return came with a caveat: that he cut off his dreadlocks he had been growing for seven years in order to film "for a day." Speaking to Zeteo, Stephens said he had even argued his case to point out that he had been wearing a helmet throughout his Rogue One appearance, which would have hidden his locks again in Andor. Alas, he was told this still would not be good enough — and Stephens walked away.
"In Rogue One, I'm wearing a helmet the whole time. So I was like, yeah I've got locks but who cares, just put me in a helmet [again]," he began.
"'Well, we're going to shoot scenes of the army training'," he claimed he was then told in response by an unknown person connected to the series' production. "'We're going to be training so we're going to need you in traditional army attire, including your hair. And if you have locks, I don't think it'd be realistic'."
To this, Stephens says he reacted incredulously, pointing out that Star Wars was far from a realistic franchise. The rapper also admitted that the offer came with "f*** all" money for his appearance.
"I was like, you're talking about an intergalactic space war with giant slugs and swords made of light, and you're worried about a soldier having dreadlocks?" he concluded. "On principal... the cognitive dissonance was too difficult to handle. The idea that someone would watch and say 'oh, well he's got dreadlocks so it's obviously not real'... what is going on? It's absolutely insane."
The hair-cutting requirement for Stephens to return meant that the muscian and actor ultimately missed out on appearing in one of the best Star Wars projects in recent years — if not all time. Andor is frequently praised by fans as being Disney's best production in the franchise, and is absolutely worth your time if you have not yet watched it to date.
Oh, and the idea that Star Wars characters can't have dreadlocks? This is clearly ridiculous, and undermined by the appearance of Jedi Master Quinlan Vos throughout the Clone Wars series — who has dreadlocks himself.
Image credit: Disney/Lucasfilm.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: GameStop and third-party resellers have raised the price of used PS5 Pros to as little as $1,400, a $500 markup on Sony's suggested retail price.
item.description:
GameStop and third-party resellers have raised the price of used PS5 Pro consoles to as much as $1,400 — a $500 markup on Sony's suggested retail price.
Last night, rumors began flying around that GameStop would be jacking up the price on pre-owned PS5 Pros to $1,399 for an all-digital PS5 Pro. That was confirmed this morning when the company's website was updated with this price point. Third-party resellers who move products through Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart have also changed their prices to similar amounts. The price hike appears to be a result of the overwhelming demand for Sony's premium console, which went from $750 to $900 earlier this year.
Demand is expected to be high for the console due to the release of GTA 6, which will most likely take advantage of the console's extra power. Sony may struggle to meet that demand due to ongoing component shortages, which in turn may have encouraged a price rise for the pre-owned market. Prices on used PS5 Pros through third-party resellers have been well over MSRP since new units began selling out earlier this year, so it seems GameStop has decided to capitalize on the opportunity.
Of course, this kind of money could get you pretty close to a nice PC, but the difference for a lot of people who are currently in the market for a new game machine is that a PC won't play GTA 6 in November. As a result, people will be forced to either pay a hefty price for a console or go without.
This is the first console generation where hardware prices have significantly increased instead of dropping, making it harder for new players to hop on board. It also raises questions about the pricing of the next console generation. As for the PS5 Pro specifically, IGN gave the console a 7/10 in 2024 and stated that its launch price tag was already a hard sell.
"The PlayStation 5 Pro is an impressive console with noticeable boosts in performance and graphics for games that take advantage of its powerful hardware," we said. "But for $700, you’ll need to think twice about whether or not the upgrade is worth the price tag."
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now available to rent or purchase digitally from VOD platforms like Prime Video.
item.description:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now available to rent or purchase digitally from VOD platforms like Prime Video.
The move to digital comes almost 70 days after Brand New Day landed in theaters, one of the longest theatrical windows of 2026. That extended time in theaters certainly paid off. The Spider-Man sequel exploded out of the gate with a record-breaking opening weekend, going on to gross over $2.5 billion over the course of its run.
That box office total includes a $951 million domestic haul that solidified Brand New Day's place as the highest-grossing movie in U.S. history. On the global front, it only trails behind Avatar and Avengers: Endgame. Of course, we’ll see what happens to those rankings when Doomsday hits.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now available to rent for $24.99 or purchase digitally for $29.99. If you choose to purchase the movie, you’ll also get bonus features.
The new Spider-Man movie picks up in the current-day timeline of MCU’s Phase 6, specifically after No Way Home, which ended with a pretty big development for Tom Holland’s Peter Parker. The sequel brings back Peter’s pals, MJ (Zendaya) and Ned (Jacob Batalon), who have now graduated high school. It also introduces new MCU cast members, most notably Sadie Sink, though Marvel tried its hardest to keep her role secret until Brand New Day hit heaters.
Tom Jorgensen’s review for IGN describes Brand New Day as a “a refreshingly small-scale ride” compared to some recent MCU projects, saying director Destin Daniel Cretton refocuses “on the sturdiest pillars of the webslinger's iconography: struggling to find balance while swinging around New York City saving the day, and looking dang cool doing it.”
While you’d assume the web-slinging hero would be leading the pack for Avengers: Doomsday, Tom Holland is actually one of the few MCU stars that hasn’t yet been confirmed to be part of the big crossover. That doesn’t mean a whole lot, however, and Marvel is reportedly working on an Avengers-style re-release of Brand New Day with extra footage.
Spider-Man 5 is already confirmed to be in the works, with an unsurprising name currently attached as the director. What isn’t attached to the project is a release date, and Marvel has a packed schedule until at least 2029. At the very least, we can look forward to the return of Sadie Sink in a full X-Men reboot slated for 2028.
Recent movies under the Disney umbrella have landed on the Disney+ streaming service between three and four months after their initial release in theaters. Assuming the latest Spider-Man movie follows a similar time, it should be available to Disney+ subscribers by late November.
Brand New Day is also getting a robust 4K Blu-ray release, including the full steelbook treatment. A spread of DVDs are now available to preorder, all of which have a release date of December 15. Just in time for the holidays.
If you're generally looking to bulk up your library, Amazon has tons of ongoing physical media deals as part of its Prime Big Deal Day sale.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Warhammer Survivors, the upcoming roguelite bullet heaven from Warhammer 40,000's Auroch Digital in partnership with Vampire Survivors' poncle, will be released on November 10, 2026, on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, PC, and mobile.
item.description:
Warhammer Survivors, the upcoming roguelite bullet heaven from Warhammer 40,000's Auroch Digital in partnership with Vampire Survivors' poncle, will be released on November 10, 2026, on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, PC, and mobile.
Warhammer Survivors launches priced $7.99 / £6.39 / €7.49 with a 10% launch and preorder discount available on select platforms. If you have Xbox Game Pass, you'll be able to play it at no extra charge on day one.
Warhammer Survivors brings together two campaigns and over 40 playable characters from the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes, and that's in addition to over 75 weapons and more than 15 stages.
I want to spend a moment on the weapons, because there are not only those you'd expect from the world of Warhammer, including Neave Blacktalon's Tempest Axes and Malum Caedo's Chainsword, but also weapons inspired by the tabletop experience we all know and love. Yes, you can hurl Nuln Oil at enemies to drench them in a substance that makes them more susceptible to fire damage, or launch D6 Dice across the stage that explode if they land on the right number.
This is made even better by the fact that there is an actual Hobby Table stage that brings it all together in a glorious way.
We had the chance to try out Warhammer Survivors, and you can not only read our preview right here, but you can also play the exact same demo right now on PC via Steam or Xbox. This new demo added The Legend of Catachan and Lyssa Ravenya alongside improvements based on community feedback from the last demo.
Warhammer Survivors will also feature Extremis Bosses like the Norn Emissary that aim to be the most challenging content "even for Survivors-like veterans," a paint pot system, and so much more.
Adam Bankhurst is a news writer for IGN. You can follow him on Twitter @AdamBankhurst and on Twitch.

item.title: Artstorm, developer of PvP naval warfare game Modern Warships, has admitted to using an independent artist’s creation as the basis for one of its ship designs.
item.description:
Artstorm, developer of PvP naval warfare game Modern Warships, has admitted to using an independent artist’s creation as the basis for one of its ship designs. The plagiarism came to light yesterday when concept artist Alex Jay Brady posted the similarities between their creation and the ship model in-game.
Brady’s art, a design for an atomic ekranoplan carrier vessel, was shown side-by-side against the in-game model in Modern Warships, called the RF Bartini A-2000-7. Even a casual onlooker could see the similarities.
I did not give @ModernWarships permission to use my ekrano design, but I have to say she's looking great. Much more detailed than my sketches. Honestly if they'd just asked and sent me some $$$$ Id have had zero issue with them using it.Its not to late to do the right thing guys https://t.co/E2K7z3rE9i
IGN reached out to Brady for more information. “For me the design is the same, with a few minor differences,” Brady said. “The location of the AWACs dish (and there being two, which I assume has something to do with the technical requirements of the game necessitating symmetry?) the number of engines etc…
“But as there never was a swing wing ekranoplan carrier (for good reason) and every detail aside from that is carried over from my design, it seems cut and dried. I have all the project files including, for example, the lines on the deck. The design makes little sense from a realism pov; the engines wash across the deck, the planes take off backward, not into the wind, I just didn't know anything about the subject when building it and they cloned all those mistakes wholesale.”
Since the tweet grew in popularity, developer Artstorm has reached out to Brady, who will consider “the issue closed” and the images added to their portfolio “as a roundabout piece of contract work” if they accept any offer made. Publisher Gaijin told IGN the Modern Warships team had responded to Brady on X, but declined to offer any more detail.
In a tweet reply to Brady, Artstorm said: “Fair call, and apologies from us. Your design was used as a reference without proper clearance. We’ll contact you directly to make this right.” Brady is currently waiting to see what the developer offers in exchange for using their work as a basis of an in-game design.
To unlock the carrier in-game, players would have to spend between $50-100 on gacha spins. Alternatively, players could purchase it with in-game currency, with the RF Bartini A-2000-7 averaging between 7,000 AC and 15,000+ AC (ArtCoins). The average cost of AC is roughly $100 for 1,300 to 2,000 AC. At this rate, a ship costing 10,000 AC would technically cost $500-700+, with a bit of wiggle either side depending on market price fluctuations.
Many Steam reviews of Modern Warships complain about the pricing of the free-to-play title’s more effective vessels. As one put it: “This game is absolutely terrible. The developers and moderators seem to be far more interested in making money from players than in making a balanced and enjoyable game. They are theives [sic].”
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: John Cena has officially ruled out a return to physical performance in the WWE, having retired from professional wrestling in December.
item.description:
John Cena has officially ruled out a return to physical performance in the WWE, having retired from professional wrestling in December.
The 17-time world champion hung up his jorts after an almost 25-year spell with the WWE following a submission defeat to Gunther in Washington, D.C. on December 13.
Since then there has been speculation from some fans that the Peacemaker actor may return to the ring, but in a new interview with the Today Show, he rubber stamped his retirement.
“I’m not going to perform again physically,” Cena declared. “There is no chance that I’ll perform again physically. And the WWE and I had a conversation about that, and we thought that at 49 it was the right time to step away. I put 23 years of physical service into the business.”
That’s that, then, for Cena’s career as a wrestler, but he’s not done with the WWE. He will return to the WWE in non-wrestling roles and as an ambassador, including the John Cena Classic in December. Cena said this live event will be based on the nostalgia for his WWE character, and the audience will decide the champion.
While Cena made a name for himself as a WWE star, he has also carved out a successful career as an actor. He has played DC anti-hero Peacemaker since 2021, including in James Gunn’s rebooted DC Universe, and there is an expectation that he will reprise the role either in an upcoming DCU movie or a potential Peacemaker Season 3. He’s currently promoting action comedy Matchbox: The Movie, which is based on the toy brand Matchbox by Mattel.
Through it all is the question of whether a WWE retirement ever be considered genuine. Wrestlers have a habit of retiring and then returning to the ring, so while Cena has officially ruled out getting physical in the WWE again, I doubt anyone would be surprised if he came back for a match or two.
Still, his latest comments echo those he issued in June last year, before his final match. "There is no way," Cena told Good Morning America at the time. "There is absolutely... I don't want to speak in absolutes, because I don't want to close any opportunity, but I made a promise to the fans who've allowed me to be here for a quarter of a century. They allowed me to sit with you today. I wouldn't want to disrespect them like that. This is an event — when people attend, it's very exclusive."
The wrestler, who is considered one of the greatest of all time, also noted that he didn’t want to “ruin” the connection he’s built with fans throughout his career for the “selfish gain” of picking back up again after announcing his decision to step back from the sport.
Photo by Michael Marques/WWE via Getty Images.

item.title: In this exclusive interview with director Jan Theysen, we go into detail on how the Space Marines actually work in Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4.
item.description:
As development on Dawn of War 4 gathers pace like the Waaagh! of a planet-cracking Ork stampede, we’re getting a better sense of exactly how the real-time strategy Warhammer 40,000 game will play. King Art Games has already published numerous gameplay videos showing off competitive multiplayer, which will be an important part of the game, but how, exactly, will the Space Marines work?
You know the Space Marines, right? The poster boys of Games Workshop's Warhammer 40,000 tabletop are more often than not the stars of the show when it comes to video game adaptations. From the Ultramarines to the Space Wolves, the Space Marines have been leading the Warhammer 40,000 video game charge from day one. Indeed, the Dawn of War series' Blood Ravens, which were created by original developer Relic Entertainment, are now firmly entrenched within the Warhammer 40,000 canon as a legit chapter of Space Marines.
In Dawn of War 4 the Blood Ravens return, but this time they have help in the form of the Dark Angels and, briefly during the campaign, their primarch, Lion El'Jonson. In this exclusive interview with director Jan Theysen, we go into detail on how the Space Marines actually work in Dawn of War 4, explore some winning strategies, and find out what sets them apart from the Necrons, Orks, and the Adeptus Mechanics. We’ve also got a batch of exclusive screenshots showing off the Space Marines in all their glory, which you can view via the slideshow below.
IGN: How would you describe the Space Marine faction in terms of how it plays and how its different from the other factions at launch?
Jan Theysen: The Space Marines are definitely the most elite faction we have in the game. You control relatively few units that are pretty expensive, but also very good in what they're doing. You don't want to lose them. You want to protect your guys, you want to upgrade them. There are a lot of different equipments and abilities and so on. If you have your small, super well-equipped Space Marine Strike Force, you really want to care about it. So, especially in the early game, you really don't want to lose one of your units.
But the good news is that in the early game no other early game unit can defeat a Space Marine. They are the big boys. But also there are few. And so that is the challenge: wherever you are you are winning, but you are not everywhere.
IGN: What would you suggest as a good strategy for the Space Marines in multiplayer?
Jan Theysen: In Skirmish and in Multiplayer, it's very important in general to get out there quickly, to capture resource points and so on. But there's a little bit of a disadvantage for Space Marines, right? Because, compared to other factions, they can't quickly capture all the different points because you don't have that many units.
But whenever you see an enemy unit, you know you can probably kill it. So one good idea would be to go out there, maybe try to recapture enemy points pretty quickly because they can't get you off of the point easily again. Be aggressive and go after the enemy and only retreat if the enemy has like, two or maybe three units attacking you. You know that at some point you might think about retreating, or you might think about, just stand your ground, maybe auto heal your unit and wait until reinforcements appear, because that is also something you can do as Space Marines. You're relatively hard to kill. And so you can basically outlast even an overwhelming attack for some time, and wait or keep everybody occupied until the reinforcements arrive.
In general, the Space Marines can build anywhere on the map and they don't need a builder unit. They just call in the buildings from orbit. And so that is something you can keep in mind. You can maybe put some of your production buildings next to resource points, or almost build a little bit of a secondary base somewhere closer to the front line maybe, so that when you produce units they are already where you need them. And you can also produce units in reserve, which basically means that instead of producing the units and then having it on the battlefield already, you have the unit in orbit and can bring it down via Drop Pod or via Thunderhawk, which gives you a lot of flexibility. Because basically, if there is a surprise attack somewhere else, or if you spotted maybe a point that is not super well defended, you can just bring more units in and really quickly capture this point. These shock and awe tactics, so to speak, is really something that Space Marines excel at.
IGN: What are some of the little details you added to the Space Marines that players will notice?
Jan Theysen: A lot has to do with equipment and weapons. So when the Space Marines level up, you can give them better weapons, but not necessarily just a straight better weapon, but you can then start to specialise them. The Intercessors, for example, you can go for longer range or for more like an Auto Bolter, which fires faster. And you can push the units in a certain direction. And this is also true if you have something like a Dreadnought. Do you want a Dreadnought that's really strong against vehicles? Or do you want a Dreadnought that’s really strong against masses of infantry? And then you might pick a Gatling gun or you might pick a plasma gun. And so basically, Space Marines are super flexible.
To me they feel like in Dawn of War 1 where you had your units where you feel like, oh, these are my anti-infantry guys, and these are my whatever, and you build this little super specialised squad. Or maybe one or two units together. And then you have your hero killers or you have your vehicle destruction crew or something like that. And that is a lot of fun.
I think in general the Space Marines are probably one of the easier factions to play because you don't have that many units you have to control at any point. And since they're not that easy to kill, they forgive if you take a couple of seconds longer to realize that you're under attack. But on the other hand, if you then lose a couple of them, or if there's like a surprise attack from the enemy, it takes longer until you get back to full speed. Because not only do you have to buy a unit again if you lost a unit, but then you also have to upgrade them. And so you really want to make sure that you keep your units alive.
IGN: In terms of animation and design, how did you approach building the Space Marines so they don’t all run around looking like Buzz Lightyear?
Jan Theysen: I think we can all agree that Space Marines look badass, but this also comes with a lot of problems when you want to animate them, right? I mean, having these huge shoulders and having really restricted movement because of the armor and so on does not make your life easier. For the animators, it's figuring out how can we make sure that they feel right in terms of, they are very strong and they are very massive, but they are also very quick. Which is a little bit of a problem, right? Because if you have someone who's just very strong, but then very slow, you can easily communicate, okay, it's like a muscle mountain and usually slow but super strong. But you also want to make them quick, right? And so it's like, okay, if they're just stronger and quicker than everybody, then they are again kind of normal humans.
How can we communicate this strength? If a Space Marine fights an Ork, or they can also fight in our game a Guard in Multiplayer or in Skirmish, then you really see the difference. Then you really see, okay, how big a Space Marine is and how powerful a Space Marine is compared to other units.
And this was also one of the reasons why we actually start the game or the tutorial with the Guards. Because we wanted to set the baseline first. Like this is normal people, normal soldiers basically. And these are Space Marines, and this is how much better the Space Marines are. Because in the end, if everybody is like a super warrior then nobody is a super warrior.
IGN: What are the most powerful endgame Space Marine units?
Jan Theysen: In general, compared to other factions, the Space Marines do not have like this one super unit at the end. But they have a strong roster all the way through. They might even be a little bit focused on infantry because they have definitely a lot of different options there, including Terminators and Bladeguards and Eliminators, so very different kinds of infantry.
But then at some point you get the Dreadnoughts, which are already nice, but then you get the tanks. We have the Gladiator in two different versions: the Lancer and the Reaper. And then we have the Redemptor Dreadnought, which is the biggest tank in the game and also one of the biggest units in the game.
But compared to, let's say, an Imperial Knight, which is what the Ad Mech gets, they are not on the same level because they are still meant to be like a unit that you use in normal battles basically, or like in normal situations. So you might have two or three Reapers, you might have two or so Redemptor Dreadnoughts, and then you have your little tank strike force there. So it's not like this, okay, you have one of those, and this is like super special, right?
IGN: Which characters are available for the Space Marines and how do they work?
Jan Theysen: The Space Marines actually have the most characters and also the most playable characters. We have two Blood Ravens and two Dark Angel characters in the game. The Blood Ravens are Cyrus, who is basically a sniper / infiltrator who can hide, and he has a very long range weapon and a lot of stuff that revolves around hiding and scouting. Then we have Jonah Orion, who is a Librarian. He, of course, has a lot of different spells and stuff he can do to AOE attack.
Then we have for the Dark Angels, Astoran, who is a Captain in Terminator armor. He is the tankiest of the commanders we have in the game. You can equip him offensively, defensively, range, melee, so he's really, really flexible. But he is always super tanky. If you put him in a group with Bladeguards or other Terminators, that's definitely a brick that's hard to kill. And then lastly we have Ezrael, who is a Chaplain on Bike. And his main thing is, first of all, he's fast because he's an Outrider, but also, he can buff and motivate, so to speak, people around him. So he's very good at making others around him fight better. But he's also really a good character for just quick interventions. Because again, as a Space Marine, you have the problem that you can't be everywhere at once, right? So attach him to a unit of Outriders and have him as a fire brigade — something is burning, go figure it out. He's very, very useful for that.
IGN: Since the last time we spoke the game was pushed back to December. What are you now able to achieve that you wouldn't have been able to otherwise?
Jan Theysen: It's not like the one big thing we still wanted to do, right? It's more like there are a bunch of different things that we got from feedback from playtests and so on, where we felt like, oh yeah, that would be good to have it, it would be nice. Also, sometimes things we said, okay, we're probably not going to put it in the launch version, but then, that's definitely a we should do later on.
And then when we talked about, okay, do we want to launch in September or December? We basically said, okay, if we start in December or, you know, late November for the preorder guys, we could just put a lot more of these nice to have, should haves, and so on into the game and also, of course, just polish everything more in terms of performance and visuals.
And, as you know, this September is very busy. So a lot of things came together. We basically said, okay, this is probably the right decision because in the end, it's less than three months later, but we think the game is a lot better because of it.
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 launches on PC on December 3, 2026.
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline, amid an explosion of AI-fueled games across the internet.
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline, amid an explosion of AI-fueled games across the internet.
Footage of GTA 5 running in a browser spread via social media yesterday, though the game's website is now offline — with reports that hosting service Cloudflare stepped in to intervene.
This latest development follows last week's cease and desist sent by Bethesda to block the AI-generated Fallout: New York fan project, which was also made playable via a PC browser. That game had been built by Claude Opus 5.5, and it seems likely that the PC build of GTA 5 was compiled similarly.
GTA 5 is now playable on web browser Here I am playing GTA 5 on chrome https://t.co/W7L7qfuI2Z
The owner of the GTA 5 browser website is now asking "Who wants the source code?" https://t.co/pEs6lLSXhP
Last week, IGN reported on the original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved, which was made available to play in a web browser. This is not a port of Bungie’s seminal 2001 first-person shooter, rather the original Xbox game running in your browser.
There's no doubting the popularity of these AI-built clones or derivative games, with images and gameplay videos being shared widely on social media alongside impressed responses from fans. But the owners of these franchises such as Rockstar and Bethesda will inevitably take a dim view of what they will likely see as piracy — particularly in the case of GTA 5's port.
Still, it remains to be seen exactly how the rapid progress of AI will be checked — or how AI-generated versions of popular games will be policed in future, beyond publishers simply playing whack-a-mole as popular examples pop up.
AI is making what was traditionally a painstaking process of reverse-engineering and recompilation significantly faster, which has prompted some to wonder about the future of commercial video game development. Why buy a Switch 2 if you can have AI generate a clone of one of Nintendo's exclusives for free in your browser?
Others, though, have pointed out that none of the "game-merging" mods or clones display any creativity or present any new ideas, rather take existing popular video games and either mash them together or simply replicate what is already playable better elsewhere.
The question for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two now is, how long will it take for GTA 6 to be made playable in a browser, and what can it do to stop it?

item.title: Ubisoft will attempt to relaunch Watch Dogs: Legion next year via a revamped Director's Cut, it's been reported.
item.description:
Ubisoft will attempt to relaunch Watch Dogs: Legion next year via a revamped Director's Cut, it's been reported.
Legion launched back in 2020 to a somewhat tepid reaction, and the once-promising franchise has subsequently been rested, with no all-new game believed to be in development. But there is a push to do more with Legion early next year, Insider Gaming has reported — something that IGN has also heard through its own sources.
Watch Dogs: Legion divided fans by ditching the series' single-protagonist focus, and instead allowing you to play as any NPC from its virtual recreation of post-Brexit London. In practice, though, that meant playing as one of various archetypes (builder, hooligan, spy) who could be killed off if you failed missions.
Later DLC added Watch Dogs 1's Aiden Pearce and Watch Dogs 2's Wrench as playable characters, before an Assassin's Creed expansion attempted to reignite interest with a fun but non-canonical crossover featuring a descendant of Assassin's Creed Syndicate's Jacob and Evie Fry.
What could Watch Dogs: Legion Director's Cut contain? It seems likely to expect the above content to be included from the off, and perhaps more of a focus on the series' more recognizable faces, rather than that ability to play as anyone — but time will tell.
Watch Dogs: Legion creative director Clint Hocking abruptly parted ways with Ubisoft earlier this year, despite being in the middle of leading development on Assassin's Creed Hexe. Subsequently, Hocking said the experience of leading a large team within Ubisoft had been like working while "flaming barrels [are] falling down from a construction site," akin to a scene from the arcade game Donkey Kong.
This month, Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot acknowledged the fact that Watch Dogs hadn't been named alongside its other major franchises as a focus for the company following its recent restructure, but said it was still considered "an important brand for the future." In the meantime, it remains unclear what is happening with the long-planned Watch Dogs movie project that wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but still lacks a release date.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Rockstar apparently isn’t interested in making a political statement in GTA 6.
item.description:
Rockstar apparently isn’t interested in making a political statement in GTA 6, a game about love, passion, and the shrinking of the American dream. In the company’s defense, its reasoning is sound. Rockstar has never been scared to push the boat, with GTA 5 famously touching on the effectiveness of torture and government blacksites, and GTA 6 will likely be no different.
The line is drawn at political satire via real-world moments. If GTA 6 had created an NPC called Melon Husk who shoots rockets into space and is a bit weird, by the time it came out it wouldn’t have factored in all the horrible stuff that character’s real-life counterpart has done since. These games take a long time to make, and no one wants to be as dated as a Borderlands gag.
"If you go back to previous GTAs, there's never really been much focus on national politics," Rupert Humphries, senior vice president of narrative of Rockstar, told Love Magazine. "The rise of Homeland Security and the Patriot Act were pretty central to GTA 4, but that was mainly because post-9/11 New York was a real frontline for those issues.
“Because we are trying to make games that feel very specific to the moment they are released, but at the same time, not reflective of the exact world we live in, we don't want to be too specific about any particular person, event, movement or anything like that.”
Instead, the focus is on capturing the essence of Florida — all the wild Florida men and women, cops and gangbangers the developer met on its GTA 6 research trips. “We have really tried to build out our world — filling it with all the characters and culture wars necessary to make it feel alive,” Humphries said.
“And then we have so many ways to tell these stories outside of actually meeting characters face to face. You can see a sign for an election, receive a robocall from a campaign, or hear a commercial on the radio. And then we have some great political talk shows on the radio too where they discuss all these issues.”
The focus is telling it all through the lens of satire, making it larger than life. Rockstar isn’t shying away from themes and contemporary topics, but rather than holding up a mirror and saying “remember this?” it’s attempting to explore those topics through its own original characters and scenarios.
GTA 6 features dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, who embark upon a crime spree across a fictionalized rendition of Florida, called Leonida in-game. Local NBA team the Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-themed uniforms in its upcoming match to celebrate the game’s upcoming launch.
GTA 6 comes to PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19, 2026. GTA 6 is expected to make up to $5.2 billion in sales by the end of launch week. The previous game continues to break records — GTA 5 has sold over 200 million copies across consoles and PC.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Following the launch of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Halo Studios has put out a blog post detailing plans for the future of Master Chief’s story. It’s an interesting look at where the series might have gone, prior to the recent announcement that Activision is now the shepherd of the Halo series.
item.description:
Following the launch of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Halo Studios has put out a blog post detailing plans for the future of Master Chief’s story. It’s an interesting look at where the series might have gone, prior to the recent announcement that Activision is now the shepherd of the Halo series.
The next Halo game was reportedly still years away, but the blog post, penned by Halo franchise writer Alex Wakeford, gives us a peek behind the curtain with hints about the studio’s plans, but also an attempt at canonizing a story that’s been told through games, remakes, books, and TV. You can check out the blog post for its list of retcons and continuity clarifications.
While the majority of the blog was written prior to the Xbox reshuffle, when Halo Studios thought the series was still in its hands, there are addendums written prior to the news breaking. At one point, Wakeford joked that you’ll have to wait until next week to find out more about the Sacristan Order, before dropping a note: “This joke sure took on new dimensions after last week's news.”
Elsewhere, Wakeford talked about the next novel by Troy Denning, titled Halo: Fireteam Noble. “Many have been asking whether this novel will still be releasing,” Wakeford said. “To this we can say that it is absolutely our intent to see this project cross the finish line. Troy has written a fantastic story and a good chunk of the editorial process has been conducted.”
Another novel, Halo: Burn the Road Home, written by senior franchise writer at Halo Studios, Kenneth Peters, is also in the works, though its future is as uncertain as Fireteam Noble. There’s no word on whether preorders will get a refund if the projects don’t make it over the line.
We also have official art of the Primordial, by Sam Wood. The Primordial would go on to become the Gravemind from Halo 2. "A creature of horrifying providence and intent known by many names — the Timeless One, the Primordial, and eventually the Gravemind," Wakeford said. "This twisted progeny of the Precursors was executed by Bornstellar through the use of a timelock on Gyre 11, reducing its form to dust by subjecting it to the passage of millions of years in mere moments. But the Primordial's experiments had borne fruit. Having infected itself with the Flood, the consciousness of this strange being passed into the parasite's hive mind where it is awakened whenever the Flood successfully form a compound intelligence."
Perhaps the most interesting bit of information for Halo lore fans comes at the end of the blog post with a tease of the Xalanyn, children of Abaddon. "THE ENDLESS EMERGE," Wakeford declared. "And finally, as is tradition, we’ll leave you with something that hopefully sparks your imagination and lets your canon curiosities run wild with endless questions."
The Xalanyn are an advanced race of immortal beings whose members were imprisoned by the Forerunners. The suggestion here is Halo 7, or whatever Halo Studios' now scrapped next Halo game would have been called, would have revealed more of the mysterious overarching antagonists.
The concept art is very cool and makes me a bit sad that Halo will probably never see them. It’s about time Halo got some new enemies to chew through. Instead, Halo will probably become Xbox’s Call of Duty (let’s pretend Call of Duty isn’t Xbox’s Call of Duty, for the sake of argument).
Halo Studios’ final game in the series was released globally on July 28, 2026, with IGN’s Halo: Campaign Evolved review praising the “gunplay that revolutionized first-person console games” which makes it still “worth playing today.” The game was a testbed for a switch to the Unreal Engine, following a middling launch for Halo Infinite, which used the studio’s proprietary Slipspace Engine.
Yesterday, people at Ninja Theory announced layoffs following the Xbox reshuffle that resulted in the studio closing down. Staff at Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition are also reportedly expecting layoffs, despite positive reviews of the studio’s latest game.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Hideo Kojima teased that he's got a cameo in a "big" live-action movie, but he's not saying which one we'll see him in quite yet.
item.description:
Hideo Kojima teased that he's got a cameo in a "big" live-action movie, but he's not saying which one we'll see him in quite yet.
The Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding creator enticed film fans to theorize about his movie career during a surprise installment in the Koji10 podcast. In between talking about Physint and what's next for his Kojima Productions, the famed game developer revealed that he would appear in movie theaters as part of a big new live-action movie cameo.
"I already shot a few other things," Kojima said, as translated through YouTube's English captions (via @Genki_JPN). "Directors and others have asked me to."
The topic came up when reminiscing about his time doing voice acting work as a mole in Zootopia 2. While the Japanese version of the Pixar film had him provide his talents behind the scenes, he suggested this mysterious new project will allow him to be in front of the camera in some capacity.
So as not to spoil the surprise, he said he "can't say" what it is yet, but it is a "big movie." It is indeed live-action, too, but his involvement is so secretive for now that he even refused to tell his hosts where he shot his part.
Kojima is best known for his work as a game developer, but he's also a well-read cinephile, too. Fans routinely turn up for his reviews of movies like Superman, Backrooms, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and more. Even his social media biography jokes that "70% of my body is made of movies," so it's no surprise to see him continue to be as involved in film as he can manage.
Many have also already started speculating when exactly we'll see Kojima show up, too, even if no one has any truly solid leads to go on yet. Some have guessed we'll see him in Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part 3 this December, while others suggested he'll show up in The Legend of Zelda movie, or even next month's Godzilla Minus Zero. Other guesses come from those who are just happy to see their favorite game creator show up in live-action at all.
"Hideo Kojima will return in Avengers: Doomsday," one fan said.
Kojima also said his future in entertainment will see him in not one but two "major anime" titles. These are "really big" but still a mystery for audiences for now, with the developer only saying that he has speaking lines coming up. He also said that an upcoming game cameo – a concept that is far from new for him – is also a secret, though fans have already found evidence that he's been scanned for Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet.
In terms of Kojima's main occupation, he's still very much at work on his new espionage action game, Physint. He offered an update on the Bill Skarsgård-starring title's progress during today's podcast, too, teasing that many of the characters' names have already been decided, and their actors scanned. He's also still heads-down working on his horror game, OD.
Photo by Rosdiana Ciaravolo/Getty Images.

item.title: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon.
item.description:
Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon.
As reported by Game File, Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot was asked by an investor about the future of the Watch Dogs franchise. The CEO noted that Ubisoft considers the IP "to be an important brand for the future" but neglected to explain how. Game File's Stephen Totilo stated that Guillemot suggested that there are no Watch Dogs games in active development at the moment, which suggests Ubisoft may still be figuring out where to take the series from here.
There is a Watch Dogs movie on the horizon, but there's no word on when it will be released. The film wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but there hasn't been any sort of meaningful promotion for the film to date. As of right now, it doesn't even have a release date, which makes it even more of a mystery.
Watch Dogs made its debut back in 2014, though it was initially meant to launch simultaneously with the PS4 in November 2013. Ubisoft hyped it up as a direct competitor to Grand Theft Auto 5, which released in September 2013. Unfortunately, many felt it was unable to reach some of its ambitions, but it still managed to make a dent in the open-world crime genre. Two years later, Ubisoft launched a much more impressive sequel set in San Francisco, but failed to keep the momentum going with its third installment.
Watch Dogs: Legion was released in 2020, also boasting ambitious ideas, such as the ability to control any NPC in the world. Unfortunately, the game received generally mixed reception from fans. Since then, there have been a lot of question marks around the future of the franchise. It seems Ubisoft wants to do more with Watch Dogs, but it may be trying to figure out how it can separate itself from a game like Grand Theft Auto 6, which is set to shake up the genre in November.
There may be more Watch Dogs games one day, but don't expect them within the next few years.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's ambitious new extraction mode, DMZ, has gotten a massive deep dive from Infinity Ward.
item.description:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's ambitious new extraction mode, DMZ, has received a massive deep dive from Infinity Ward.
DMZ was initially introduced in 2022's Modern Warfare II, and now, with the rise in popularity of extraction shooters, it is coming back in a bigger way. The mode is expected to be a major part of Modern Warfare 4's offerings, with its own 70-level progression system, lucrative rewards, and world building/lore. Additionally, there will be a forward operating base for players to hang out in between matches. Here, players can practice at a firing range to test their loadouts, craft items based on loot they've found in the world, gain intel and track different missions, bosses, and unique challenges for their next deployment, and more.
Speaking in a new behind-the-scenes video, Infinity Ward co-studio head Jack O'Hara stated that fans made it clear that there weren't high enough stakes in the first iteration of DMZ, so they've worked to change that. For starters, your time in DMZ is defined by your operator. This is a character that you build and level up, but if they die, it will cost you to bring them back. There are also lootable items that can be permanently lost if the player dies or drops them. These items can be used at a 3D printer to craft things like armor plates, consumables, gear, and seemingly killstreaks or AI-controlled fire support, based on a menu seen in some gameplay.
The team behind DMZ also described it as an "action extraction shooter." Infinity Ward wants players to feel like there is constant danger both through AI combatants, bosses, and other players, so you won't spend a ton of time wandering around opening boxes with minimal friction. Infinity Ward laid out a plethora of different enemy types in a blog post, noting that there will be drones, helicopter and vehicle patrols, tanks, and tougher enemies.
Different parts of the map will have different threat levels, and those levels can rise based on the player's actions. If you're running around causing a bunch of noise, it will create more attention and lead to enemies searching for you. However, if you play stealtihly with silenced weapons, melee takedowns, and exercise caution, you can avoid extreme conflict. Additionally, the more players explore, the more opportunities there will be to uncover loot and secrets in the game's world.
Infinity Ward has also promised extensive support for DMZ post-launch, including changes to the map, dynamic weather that can vary per season, and much more. It sounds like a big focus for the team and it should be a really cool change for Call of Duty. Hopefully it sticks and isn't dropped next year, but that will likely depend on if players show up to support it.
DMZ will be available at launch when Modern Warfare 4 releases on October 23. Unlike MWII's version, it will not be free-to-play.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: RuneScape developer Jagex has pulled a new trailer after a six-fingered knight led to allegations of generative AI use from fans.
item.description:
RuneScape developer Jagex has pulled a new trailer after a six-fingered knight led to allegations of generative AI usage from fans.
There were some ups and downs for RuneScape players over the weekend. What started with a string of big reveals from RuneFest 2026 ended with social media users voicing their concern that generative AI had been used to make the new trailer for RuneScape 3's Dragon Slayer 2 quest.
The backlash was loud enough that Jagex stepped in not only to release an official response on the matter but also to pull the trailer entirely while it investigates "urgently." The statement, posted on Reddit by social media manager Alex Sween (via Kotaku), acknowledged some of the more undeniable concerns related to the trailer – including the fact that one of its knights has six fingers.
"Hello, it’s me, again, talking about Gen AI, again," the statement began, referencing a separate, recent incident involving 100 Thieves and OSRS. The team also took a "hard line stance" against generative AI earlier this year. "We’re aware of the concerns raised about the Dragon Slayer 2 trailer and have taken it down, while we investigate urgently. This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used. But, among other things, there’s a sixth finger and, well, that’s pretty hard to explain away. For that we apologise.
Although uploads of RuneScape's Dragon Slayer 2 trailer can no longer be found on official channels, it is still available via the full RuneFest 2026 livestream. There are also plenty of posts from fans discussing the matter still live across social media. They're not happy, but Jagex knows that.
The team took its statement and apology as an opportunity to, again, make its position clear: "We don't use GenAI to create our games, artwork, or creative assets and will not knowingly allow it to be used on our behalf." However, it's hard to deny that a second instance of artificial intelligence being used to generate content suggests a deeper problem for the MMO developer. Jagex explained that it plans to address its approach to working with partners going forward.
Then today, Jagex decided to use AI in a trailer for an upcoming quest, the knight in video has 6 fingers and boots in a another frame look like modern sneakers.https://t.co/L6w4yotJw0 https://t.co/C9kMM2oC7c
"Immediately following RuneFest we’re overhauling our review processes," the statement continued, "and we’re going to work with and commission creators from the community to make sure that the story of Dragon Slayer 2 is told to the standard befitting of such an update."
The six-fingered knight really does feel like the smoking gun, but another bizarre piece of art from the trailer, which showed a fully-armored knight wearing what seemed to be a regular old pair of tennis shoes, had fans raising eyebrows, too. In follow-up replies, Sween acknowledged it's something Jagex "should have caught," adding, "We didn't do well enough and can't simply place the blame elsewhere."
As Jagex refines its processes to maintain its stance against generative AI, it's still working to deliver other new projects. RuneScape 4 is one of these new projects, with an animated adaptation also in the works with YouTuber MoistCr1tikal.

item.title: New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and gives them a set of new bathing suit skins.
item.description:
New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and gives them a set of new bathing suit skins.
Half the fun of Square Enix's remake trilogy is allowing Cloud, Barret, Tifa, and the rest of the party to have some fun on their way to stop Sephiroth once and for all. In Rebirth, that meant spending a day at the beach, and in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, players will be able to kick their feet up, mingle, and, for some reason, balance rubber Chocobos at a collection of new hot springs.
The publisher unveiled the new gameplay feature as part of SDCC Málaga and later shared gameplay footage on social media. When the group stops at a hot spring, they'll benefit from a permanent increase to their max HP. The health bonus and moments shared between each character seem to be the real draw. The thing that might appeal to some players more than others, though, is the promise that the bathing suit outfits featured during these segments can be unlocked as skins, too.
【名湯めぐりの旅🐤】冒険の合間に、ほっとひと息。#FF7リベレーション のワールドマップに隠された温泉スポット♨旅の仲間たちとのここでしか聞けない特別な会話が楽しめます。さらに最大HPアップの効果や衣装スキンが手に入ることも https://t.co/S41hqabFqp
Across all of the clips shown online today, we can see skins for Cloud, Barret, and Cid. Red XIII can relax in the hot springs, too, but considering he's not usually wearing clothes to begin with, it doesn't look like any skin he may get will change his appearance too much. Then, there's newly playable party member Vincent Valentine, who prefers to bathe in the same slick get-up he fights monsters in because he's… just that cool, I guess.
"We’re sharing a preview of some of the hot spring events revealed during our stage presentation at SDCC Málaga," director Naoki Hamaguchi said in a follow-up post on X/Twitter. "Each hot spring offers a different glimpse into the characters’ everyday lives, and the outfits featured in these events can also be unlocked as skins. Explore the world, discover hot springs, and enjoy these special moments with your companions!"
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is still months from delivering the concluding chapter of the remake trilogy, but that hasn't stopped Square Enix from unloading new details as often as it can manage. Hamaguchi has been especially keen to share, telling IGN last month that players will have an option to automatically level up their characters if they want to skip the grind. He's also said players could easily spend more than 100 hours playing through the story, even if the Platinum Trophy doesn't present much of a challenge on its own.
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S April 8, 2027. While we wait to see how those hot springs heat things up for Cloud and company, you can see how Hamaguchi responded to players hoping for a full-disc release. You can also check out IGN's hands-on preview.

item.title: Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and development updates on Physint, his upcoming next-generation action-espionage game and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid.
item.description:
Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and development updates on Physint, his upcoming next-generation action-espionage game and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid.
Thanks to a summary of the 79-minute English-subtitled podcast on YouTube by X user Genki_JPN, we now know a bit more about the status of Physint, which made huge headlines recently after Kojima revealed that Sony was set to cancel the project as its publisher, leading to Microsoft picking it up. Kojima describes Physint as a project to commemorate his 40th anniversary as a game developer. He said he wants it to evoke the roots of the Metal Gear Solid games, but be a new interactive experience with a different kind of spy action. He aims to fill it with lots of new ideas.
Story and cast-wise, Kojima says he has the plot already and that he pitched all of the actors appearing in it himself – 70% of whom are apparently Kojima fans. Many of the character names have been decided Filming will start next year, with Bill Skarsgard, Charlie Fraser and Minami Hamabe already scanned.
Finally, the 63-year-old Kojima said that he makes every one of his games as if it could be his last.
The other game Kojima is developing for Microsoft, the PT spiritual successor OD, is expected to be released before Physint, which Kojima himself said was 5-6 years away last year.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance studio co-founder Martin Klima is "bored and tired" of RPGs that are just "power fantasy" trips "for teenagers."
item.description:
Kingdom Come: Deliverance studio co-founder Martin Klima is "bored and tired" of RPGs that are just "power fantasy" trips "for teenagers."
The Warhorse Studios developer shared his thoughts about his least favorite kind of RPG during an interview with PC Gamer. Kingdom Come: Deliverance has received praise for straying from the beaten path in the past, and Klima's comments suggest that's no accident.
He admitted that the role-playing genre is one he enjoys. What he doesn't enjoy are the RPGs that set the player up to be "the chosen one" with a "grand task of saving the universe." It's a straightforward set-up that he's "bored and tired" of seeing, calling these kinds of experiences "repetitive."
"It's really a distillation of what the common RPG is," Klima said. "So, I found that there must be many, many people who are really tired of this formula and who want something new and different."
He continued: "The games that were and sort of are being made are still the games for teenagers. If you are 16, 17, you love playing these power fantasy games because it's something that you need. But the audience is much older today … everybody's going to think that I am hating on Expedition 33 right now, but that's definitely not the case."
There is no doubt a section of RPG fans who would agree with Klima's assessment. The question, though, remains: Why? He believes a reliance on strategies and designs that have worked in the past is to blame, saying major publishers are "best at recycling the same formula over and over."
Ubisoft is one of the more specific examples that came to mind. He called the "craftsmanship" of the publisher's games "excellent," pointing out that its games are mostly free of bugs and feature standout animations and character models. He'd prefer if that same level of craftsmanship was used on more innovative ideas, even if he doesn't have "any easy answers" for a company that could be taking financial risks when experimenting at that level.
"I played the original Assassin's Creed, and the original Far Cry, and the original Watch Dogs, and most of these games in the first iterations, and it was fun," he added. "But once you play the same game for the 10th time, it sort of becomes stale."
Klima recently commented on how he hopes GTA 6 will be able to "blaze a trail" for increased game prices. IGN reviewed Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 when it came out last year and gave it a 9/10.

item.title: The Coalition was able to work some magic on the Xbox Series S by tapping into the SSD to increase performance.
item.description:
While Gears of War: E-Day is a beautiful game, it's incredibly demanding, whether you're playing it on the Xbox Series X or on PC. But, The Coalition was able to work some magic on the Xbox Series S by tapping into the SSD to increase performance.
The Coalition's studio technical director Kate Raynor talked to Digital Foundry and described tapping into the SSD while the Series S was out of memory. That's important for a game as demanding as Gears of War: E-Day, as the Xbox Series S only has 10GB of RAM, rather than the 16GB on the Series X.
Offloading data from the RAM to an SSD is nothing new. Your computer does it all the time when you run out of memory. What happens then is that the computer relies on the Page File, a dedicated block of storage on your SSD or hard drive that's used to hold overflow data. The problem with relying on that typically, though, is that SSDs are way slower than RAM, which is why your computer slows to a halt whenever it has to lean on the Page File.
The key for Gears of War: E-Day, then, was strategically choosing which data to offload to the SSD, and which data to keep in the faster system memory. According to Digital Foundry, The Coalition got around this by prioritizing data that wasn't used "in a frame or over a run of frames," while data that's constantly needed stays in RAM.
This approach does have its limits, though, and will degrade performance over time if the page file is refreshed into memory too often – as that does have a performance cost on its own. But, with this memory trick and dropping Lumen reflections, The Coalition was able to get Gears of War: E-Day running pretty well on the Xbox Series S. Hopefully, more developers are able to adopt this approach going forward, because I have a feeling that the cheaper hardware in the Xbox Series X is going to be more necessary as the RAM crisis carries on.
Gears of War: E-Day launched last week into early access, and has some pretty big changes over past games. But, still, The Coalition is proud that Gears of War: E-Day is now one of Xbox's main exclusives.
